name: Live Skull
label: Homestead
lede: Mark C. and Tom Paine left San Francisco for downtown New York, split the singing three ways and made a band loud enough for Gowanus. In 1987 Thalia Zedek, whose band Uzi had just ended, took over the lead vocal.

eras.title: Two guitarists leave San Francisco for downtown
eras.text: Mark C. and Tom Paine build a band around twin guitars and three people sharing the vocals, in the same downtown scene as Sonic Youth and Swans.

years.src: Wikipedia: Live Skull · Trouser Press: Live Skull
years.h: Mark C. and Tom Paine, late of San Francisco's Crop, start Live Skull
years.p: Both had played in Crop before moving east in 1980. Drummer James Lo and bassist Marnie Greenholz filled out the band.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Crop also included brothers Ivan and Andrew Nahem, later of [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]]. The first Live Skull lineup had Julie Hair on vocals and Dan Braun on drums. Lo and Greenholz took over quickly, and the lead vocals split three ways between Mark C., Greenholz and Paine.

Braun went on to play with Swans and appears on their 1991 album Body to Body, Job to Job. Trouser Press files Live Skull with the avant-noisy New York scene that also produced [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], Lydia Lunch and Swans.

years.h: A self-produced EP, Live Skull, on Massive Records
years.p: Cut at Plaza Sound in New York in August 1983 and released in 1984 as Fat 1. Six songs, under 19 minutes.
years.xp: Desire Records in France reissued it on CD and LP in 2013 with eight bonus tracks, live recordings and unreleased material among them.

eras.title: Gerard Cosloy's label, Martin Bisi's room
eras.text: Two studio albums and a live record for Cosloy's Homestead, the second studio album cut at Bisi's B.C. Studio in Gowanus.

years.cap: Flyer for a CBGB bill with Sonic Youth, Volcano Suns and Hope, Friday the 24th, c. 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Bringing Home the Bait · Wikipedia: Homestead Records
years.h: Homestead puts out the first album, Bringing Home the Bait
years.p: Twelve songs in 39 minutes, recorded in 1984 at Evergreen Studio in New York with the band producing.
years.xp:
It came out as Homestead HMS 022. Homestead was a sublabel of the Dutch East India distributor, run by [[Gerard Cosloy|b3c600d5-e1dd-4525-855d-6d4f950c3be6]] from 1984 to 1990. Wikipedia notes the label became known for poor communication with artists and for not paying royalties.

Desire Records reissued the album in France in 2013 with seven bonus tracks.

years.cap: Live Skull's four-piece lineup: Mark C., Marnie Greenholz, James Lo and Tom Paine
years.src: Wikipedia: Cloud One (album) · Wikipedia: Martin Bisi · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Bisi's Gowanus studio is where Cloud One gets cut
years.p: Cut in fall 1985 and released in 1986 as Homestead HMS 056, with tighter song structures than the debut.
years.xp:
Bisi opened the studio in 1981 with Bill Laswell and Brian Eno, and Live Skull, Sonic Youth and Swans all made records there. Live Skull went back for Dusted and Positraction.

Desire Records reissued Cloud One in France in 2014, adding eight bonus tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Don't Get Any on You
years.h: A November 1986 night at CBGB becomes Don't Get Any on You
years.p: Ten tracks, among them "Debbie's Headache" and a six-minute cover of Curtis Mayfield's "Pusherman". Homestead released it in 1987 as HMS 083.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the recording to a November 1986 show at CBGB. "Pusherman" also turns up as a bonus track on the CD reissue of Dusted.

The video is a different CBGB night, the full set from July 13, 1986, with the original lineup of Mark C., Paine, Greenholz and Lo.

eras.title: Thalia Zedek takes the mic
eras.text: Thalia Zedek arrives, Richard Hutchins takes over the drums and Sonda Andersson later the bass, and the band makes Dusted and Positraction before it stops.

years.cap: Live Skull with Thalia Zedek, promo photo, c. 1987
years.src: Wikipedia: Uzi (band) · Thalia Zedek: media · Trouser Press: Live Skull
years.h: "You're Thalia Zedek!" says Mark C., and Uzi's singer has a new band
years.p: Uzi ended in 1987 after one EP. Zedek moved to New York as lead singer, and ex-Ruin drummer Richard Hutchins replaced James Lo.
years.xp:
Uzi's only record, the 1986 EP Sleep Asylum on Homestead, placed No. 5 in the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll. Mark C. says Live Skull had been playing Uzi tapes on the road, so when Zedek mentioned the band, his reaction was "You're Thalia Zedek!"

He describes her singing as talking, shouting and melody at once. Trouser Press calls her "the perfect sparkplug for Live Skull."

The video is a WNYU radio interview from September 19, 1987, in the band's first months with her.

years.cap: Thalia Zedek and drummer Rich Hutchins, Brookline, Massachusetts
years.src: Wikipedia: Dusted (Live Skull album) · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Robert Palmer of the New York Times puts Dusted on his ten best
years.p: Thalia Zedek's first record with the band, cut at B.C. Studio in mid-1987: eleven songs in under 37 minutes.
years.xp:
Wikipedia also lists Dusted at No. 29 on Melody Maker's 1988 Albums of the Year. The album's "5-D" video later appeared on the Atavistic compilation Twelve O'Clock High.

Homestead's US release carried catalog number HMS 090.

years.src: Wikipedia: Snuffer (EP) · Trouser Press: Live Skull
years.h: Caroline Records releases Snuffer, six songs with one-word titles
years.p: "Was," "Face," "Chair," "Step," "Word" and "Straw" were cut at B.C. Studio in January 1988 and released on Caroline Records.
years.xp: Trouser Press says the vocals were integrated "much better" by this record. The six songs were later added to the CD reissue of Positraction as bonus tracks.

years.cap: Flyer for Live Skull at Stache's, Columbus, Ohio, May 17, 1989, with a band photo of the Zedek, Andersson and Hutchins lineup
q: That whole album is basically one song.
years.src: Wikipedia: Positraction (album) · Thalia Zedek: media · Wikipedia: Live Skull
yt: Full show, Fort Worth, Texas, April 1989
years.h: Positraction lands on Caroline with a new bassist
years.p: Sonda Andersson, ex-Rat At Rat R, plays bass after Marnie Greenholz left in 1988.
years.xp:
Martin Bisi and the band co-produced at B.C. Studio, and it runs 32 minutes. Wikipedia says Andersson is a cousin of composer [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]].

Spin called it "a festering, appropriately black-colored slab of grinding, slash 'n' drone, East Village-trash-shit noisecluster rock."

The video is a full show in Fort Worth, Texas, on April 22, 1989, with Zedek, Andersson and Hutchins.

years.cap: Back cover of Positraction, the last Live Skull album
years.src: Wikipedia: Live Skull · Wikipedia: Thalia Zedek
years.h: Live Skull ends with Positraction, and the sources disagree on why
years.p: Wikipedia gives "sustained lack of commercial success" as the reason, and has Tom Paine leaving music for film.
years.xp:
Paine later earned an MFA in film at the University of South Florida and writes about world cinema. Wikipedia's page on Thalia Zedek puts the split down to conflicts instead, and the sources don't agree, so both are given.

Mark C. kept going in Spoiler, Int'l Shades (with ex-Sonic Youth drummer Bob Bert) and Outpost 13. Zedek headed for Boston and formed Come.

eras.title: Zedek goes back to Boston and starts Come
eras.text: With Chris Brokaw she forms Come, which lands on Matador, while Live Skull stays quiet for a quarter century.

years.src: Wikipedia: Come (American band) · Wikipedia: Chris Brokaw
years.h: Thalia Zedek and Chris Brokaw start Come in Boston
years.p: Brokaw, ex-drummer of Codeine, switched to guitar. Their seven-minute single "Car" was a Sub Pop Singles Club release.
years.xp: Zedek had known Brokaw since the mid-1980s. Wikipedia lists Sean O'Brien and Arthur Johnson as the other founders, and puts the band's start in Boston in 1990.

years.src: Wikipedia: 11:11 (Come album) · Wikipedia: Come (American band) · Thalia Zedek: media
years.h: Come spends seven and a half days at Fort Apache on 11:11
years.p: Rolling Stone's later verdict. Recorded in Cambridge in July 1992 with Tim O'Heir and Carl Plaster, out on Matador December 1.
years.xp:
The title came from the band repeatedly noticing the time on a digital clock. Chris Brokaw called it "a sort of superstitious mantra." Wikipedia says Kurt Cobain, J Mascis and Bob Mould all endorsed the band.

Mark C. says that watching Come at soundcheck, they held the room with one song.

years.src: Wikipedia: Come (American band) · Wikipedia: Thalia Zedek
years.h: After Gently, Down the Stream, Come goes quiet
years.p: It was Come's last album for Matador. Zedek and Brokaw went solo, and her Been Here and Gone came out on Matador on July 31, 2001.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Come page says the band paused after 1998. Come played a two-song set at Boston's Middle East in November 2007, a full reunion at Spain's Tanned Tin Festival in November 2008, and toured for 11:11's 20th anniversary in May and June 2013. Zedek's own page dates Come's end to 2001.

eras.title: Back in the room where it started
eras.text: French reissues, a reunion at Bisi's studio, and three new albums from a band that hadn't made one since 1989.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bringing Home the Bait · Wikipedia: Cloud One (album) · Wikipedia: Live Skull (EP)
years.h: Desire Records, in France, reissues the first three Live Skull records
years.p: Live Skull and Bringing Home the Bait came out in 2013 and Cloud One in 2014, each with bonus tracks.
years.xp: Each CD adds live cuts and unreleased songs: seven extras on Bait, eight on both Cloud One and the EP.

years.src: New York Music Daily: A Historic Marathon Weekend · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Three of the old band play B.C. Studio for the first time since 1988
years.p: Mark C., Marnie Greenholz and Rich Hutchins came back to the room where they recorded three albums, for the studio's 35th anniversary.
years.xp: New York Music Daily called it the band's first public performance together since 1988, in the same space. Tom Paine was not there. Wikipedia describes the night as a semi-private "Recording of the Century" event where they played and recorded new songs.

years.src: Live Skull Bandcamp: Saturday Night Massacre · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.p: Ten tracks on Bronson Recordings, with Thalia Zedek and Greenholz guesting and Kent Heine on bass.
years.xp:
The band says its old horror imagery gave way to something plainer: in their words, "the facts are gory enough on their own." The Wire heard some of the "scuzzy energy" of the Reagan-era peak.

Dave Hollinghurst joined on guitar in 2019, and Dangerous Visions (2020) and Party Zero (2023) followed on the same label. Colyn Hunt replaced Heine on bass in 2024.
